plugins/sinks/_remote_object_effects.py:: except OSError around path.unlink(missing_ok=True), logged and swallowed. The path is Tier-1: it is always the effect-addressed spool file ELSPETH itself created under _stage_path(effect_id, provider), never a user or provider path. Every call site has already settled the effect's primary outcome before this runs: the failure paths (_write_stage's except BaseException, the collision raise, the diversion-attribution raise, restage_remote_object's divergence raise) are in the middle of raising it, and the success paths (virtual/inherited/reaffirmed NO_PUBLICATION plans, remote_commit_result after the provider durably confirmed the conditional write, reconcile_remote_observation on an exact match) have a durable plan or provider confirmation as the outcome. Raising here would either chain a spool-hygiene error over the real cause or turn a provider-confirmed commit into a failed effect that the next re-drive reconciles as applied anyway. A leftover stage cannot be published under this effect: validate_remote_plan re-derives the plan hash from the evidence, and both remote sinks stream the stage under the plan's sealed checksum (S3 ChecksumSHA256 from evidence.staged_hash, Azure content_md5 from evidence.checksum_b64), so a divergent body is rejected by the provider before it lands. No row's accepted/diverted disposition depends on the unlink succeeding.

except OSError: continue around path.lstat() in the bounded sweep of crashed-write '.<stage>.<tmp>.building' temp bodies. The paths are Tier-1 (parent.glob over ELSPETH's own 0o700 spool directory, a glob disjoint from any stage a plan references). An lstat failure here means a concurrent effect's mkstemp/replace or a sibling process's sweep already removed or is holding the orphan; skipping it is the function's contract, which returns only the count it actually removed and never claims a skipped entry. The sweep runs from _write_stage before the calling effect has staged a single byte, so no row disposition depends on it, and raising would fail an unrelated effect's prepare because a previous crashed run's garbage could not be stat'ed.

except OSError: continue around path.unlink() of a temp body that lstat just proved is a regular file older than the stale threshold. Same Tier-1 spool path as the lstat handler; the unlink races the same concurrent sweep, and an ENOENT/EACCES here means the orphan is gone or held by someone else. The removed counter is only incremented on the successful branch, so the return value stays honest. The orphan is never referenced by any durable plan (plans name the visible '{effect_id}.body' stage, not the '.building' temp), so leaving it costs bounded disk and nothing about effect outcomes; raising would fail the calling effect's prepare for a file it does not own.
